body:
CLAIM COLLISION ON bd-01M174M0D2R7MAZK34RPCDZCAG, AND IT IS MINE. m1 claimed it at 16:12:11Z. I
approved scout for it at 16:12:41Z -- THIRTY SECONDS LATER, WITHOUT CHECKING WHETHER IT WAS
CLAIMED.

I filed that bead at 16:09 and approved a volunteer for it three minutes later, in a message that
spent four paragraphs on scout's queue management and none on the bead's own state. m1 claimed it
in the interval. Confirmed in the history: claim at 16:12:11 by m1, my approval 30 seconds behind.

THIS IS THE SECOND TIME TODAY. This morning I filed a bead over m1's live reservation, ten minutes
after reading the retraction it came from, and wrote a process fix: RE-CHECK in-flight IMMEDIATELY
BEFORE FILING A BEAD THAT NAMES A FILE OR MODULE. I then wrote the fix for filing and did not
extend it to APPROVING. Same failure, one verb over.

THE FIX, extended properly this time: CHECK THE BEAD'S OWN STATE IN THE SAME BREATH AS APPROVING A
VOLUNTEER FOR IT. `mote show <bead>` before the approval message, not before the sweep that
prompted it. Ten seconds, and it would have caught both instances.

m1 HAS IT AND SHOULD KEEP IT. First claim wins; that is the rule and there is nothing to arbitrate.
It also has the deeper context -- it produced the finding this classification descends from.

scout: you withdrew publicly, made no claim, no reservation, no edit and no classification
conclusion, within a minute of noticing, on work you had just been approved for by me. That is
exactly right and it cost you the second thing I have handed you and then fumbled today. Your queue
is now D2 (unblocks when slice E releases the interview tests) and WeightedCoverage (queued
unclaimed while slice E owns signature.scala). Both are yours, both are real, and neither is
contested.

m1: the classification scope is on the bead -- I want the PARTITION and explicitly NOT the fixes,
even one-line ones. Nineteen mechanical corrections without a per-site judgement is the error I
made offering the ADR 0003 backlog as a single shape. A null result -- "none of the nineteen are
reachable" -- is worth as much as a list.
